issues.quote: He came into the library at thirty-two minutes past ten by my watch. He said he wanted a word, and then he sat down and we sat together there until the temple struck eleven.
issues.fact: F6 says Bastien Girard came into the library at 10:32 by Félix's watch. The transcript never names him in this answer. The question asked was 'Did anyone come to the library?', and the nearest male referents are the uncle, who was the last 'he' mentioned ('I thought he had dropped something heavy', 'He had been four years on that watch'), and the uncle is the one who 'wants a word' and 'was not in a good humour'.
issues.misreading: A solver could read 'He came into the library' as the uncle, Aurèle, coming down to the library at 10:32. That would put the uncle in the library at 10:32 and contradict the thump and repeater timeline (he would have been in the atelier at 10:18). The sheet says it was Girard.

issues.quote: It has given me trouble for ten years and I have never let anyone near it, my uncle included.
issues.fact: The fact sheet says nothing about the watch being unreliable or having a fault. It only gives the readings Félix took by it.
issues.misreading: A solver could take this as a hint that the watch runs erratically and so distrust the 9:40, 9:40-type readings, or doubt the consistency of the 20-minute offset. The sheet does not support that doubt.
